raw_text:
Here’s the full 12-week plan summary, integrating resistance training, upgraded Phase 2 intensity, aerobic conditioning, mobility (non-heated), cooling strategies, and a perimenopause- and bone-health–supportive nutrition plan. Start date: 2026-06-01.

Global framework
- Weekly split: 4 lifting days + 2 aerobic sessions (Zone 2 and intervals/tempo) + 1 optional easy Z1/mobility day + 1 full rest day.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy/structural robustness; Week 4 deload.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Max strength + power with intensified loading; Week 8 deload.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength-endurance/performance; Week 12 taper/testing.
- Heat safety: No sauna or hot yoga; no fasted HIIT. Train in cool environments. Use Cooling Protocol every session.
- Autoregulation: RPE 6–9; reduce sets by 10–20% and cap at RPE 7 on high-symptom/poor-sleep days. Velocity cutoffs in Phase 2.
- Conditioning placement: Keep intervals ≥24 h from heavy squat/deadlift. If symptoms high, swap intervals for Zone 2.

Cooling protocol (all sessions)
- Pre: 500 ml cool water + electrolytes; 5–10 min neck/upper back cooling; optional menthol rinse.
- During: 150–250 ml water every 10–15 min; palm and neck cooling 60–90 s between hard sets.
- Post: 5–10 min easy walk; cool shower/neck cooling; 500–750 ml fluids with sodium.

Nutrition plan (summary)
- Calories: Maintenance to slight surplus for strength; if fat loss desired, small deficit (−5 to −10%) on 3–4 non-consecutive days only when sleep/symptoms stable.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day in 4 feedings; 0.4–0.55 g/kg per meal; 20–30 g pre-bed.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day baseline (up to 5–6 g/kg on heavy days); 30–60 g carbs pre-lift; 60–90 g post with 30–45 g protein.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day emphasizing EVOO, nuts/seeds, oily fish.
- Bone health: Calcium 1,200 mg/day (food first), Vitamin D 800–2,000 IU/day per GP, magnesium 300–400 mg/day, K2 from foods, adequate potassium. Optional 10–15 g collagen + 50 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-lifting.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day fluids; 300–600 mg sodium/L during training. Moderate caffeine, limit alcohol if it worsens hot flashes.
- Symptom support: Include soy, flax, legumes; omega-3s 2–3x/week or 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day.

Warm-up (10–12 min)
- 3–5 min easy cardio (cool room), then 2 rounds of thoracic rotations, 90/90 hip switches, band pull-aparts, glute bridges, dead bug/Pallof. Ramp-up sets to working load.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy/structural robustness
Week 1 (Jun 1–7)
- Day 1 Lower (Squat): Back Squat 4x6 @ RPE 7; RDL 3x8; Split Squat 3x8/side; Leg Curl 3x10; Calf 3x10–12; Pallof 3x12/side.
- Day 2 Upper (Horizontal): Bench 4x6 @ 7; 1-Arm DB Row 3x8–10; Incline DB Press 3x8; Rear Delt Fly 3x12; Face Pull 3x12–15; Dead Bug 3x8/side.
- Day 3 Aerobic (Intervals): 8x60 s @ RPE 7–8 / 90 s easy; total ~35 min in cool room. Mobility 10 min.
- Day 4 Lower (Hinge): Deadlift 4x4 @ 7; FFE Split Squat 3x10/side; Hip Thrust 3x8; Leg Ext 3x12; Seated Calf 3x12–15; Side Plank 3x30–45 s.
- Day 5 Upper (Vertical): OHP 4x5 @ 7; Weighted Pull-Up/Pulldown 4x6–8; DB Arnold 3x10; Cable Row 3x10; High-to-Low Fly 3x12; Ab Wheel 3x8–10.
- Optional Day 6: Zone 2 30–40 min + 15 min mobility. Day 7: Rest.

Week 2 (Jun 8–14)
- Progress 2.5–5% load or +1 rep/set at RPE 7–8. Keep session order flexible per symptoms.

Week 3 (Jun 15–21)
- Main lifts: Top set @ RPE 8 then 3 back-offs @ 7. Add one accessory set to primary accessories.

Week 4 (Jun 22–28) Deload
- 80–85% of Week 3 loads; reduce accessory sets; swap intervals for 25–35 min Zone 2.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Max strength + power (intensified)
General: Use top singles @ RPE 8–8.5; back-off sets @ RPE 8–9 with velocity cutoffs. Power primers first. Strict cooling between heavy sets.

Week 5 (Jun 29–Jul 5)
- Day 1 Lower: Jumps 5x3; Back Squat 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 4x3 @ 8–8.5; RDL 4x5 @ 8; Walking Lunge 3x8/side; Copenhagen 3x25–35 s/side.
- Day 2 Upper: Speed Bench 6x3 @ ~60%; Bench 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 4x3 @ 8–8.5; Weighted Pull-Up 4x4–5 @ 8–9; DB Incline 3x6–8 @ 8; Chest-Supported Row 3x8 @ 8.
- Day 3 Aerobic (Intervals): 7x90 s @ RPE 8–8.5 / 2 min easy.
- Day 4 Lower Hinge: Deadlift 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 5x2 @ 8.5; Front/Safety Squat 4x4 @ 8; Hip Thrust 4x5–6 @ 8–8.5; Ham Curl 3x8–10 @ 8.
- Day 5 Upper: OHP 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 5x2 @ 8–8.5; Pendlay Row 4x4–5 @ 8–9; Close-Grip Bench 3x4–6 @ 8–8.5; Lat Pulldown 3x8 @ 8.
- Optional Day 6: Zone 2 30–40 min + mobility. Day 7: Rest.

Week 6 (Jul 6–12)
- Small overload if barspeed/RPE allow (+1–2% load, or +1 back-off set).
- Day 1 Lower: Jumps 5x3; Back Squat 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 5x3 @ 8.5; RDL 4x5 @ 8–8.5; Lunge 3x8/side @ 8.
- Day 2 Upper: Speed Bench 6x3 @ 60–65%; Bench 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 5x3 @ 8.5; Weighted Pull-Up 5x4 @ 8–9; DB Incline 3x6–8 @ 8–8.5; Row 3x8 @ 8.
- Day 3 Aerobic: Option A 3x6 min @ RPE 7.5–8 (3 min Z2 between) or Option B 40–45 min Zone 2 if legs cooked.
- Day 4 Lower Hinge: Deadlift 1x1 @ 8–8.5, then 5x2 @ 8.5–9; Front/Safety 4x4 @ 8–8.5; Hip Thrust 4x5–6 @ 8.5; Ham Curl 3x8–10 @ 8.

- Optional Day 6: Zone 2 30–40 min. Day 7: Rest.

Week 7 (Jul 13–19) Peak
- Day 1 Lower: Jumps 4x3; Back Squat 2x1 @ 8.5, then 4x2–3 @ 8.5–9; RDL 3x4–5 @ 8.5; Split Squat 2x6–8/side @ 8.
- Day 2 Upper: Speed Bench 4x3; Bench 2x1 @ 8.5, then 4x2–3 @ 8.5–9; Weighted Pull-Up 4x3–4 @ 9; Chest-Supported Row 3x6–8 @ 8.5.
- Day 3 Aerobic: 5x2 min @ RPE 8–8.5 / 2 min easy (or 30–35 min Zone 2 if symptoms).
- Day 4 Lower Hinge: Deadlift 2x1 @ 8.5, then 4x2 @ 8.5–9; Front/Safety 3x3–4 @ 8.5; Hip Thrust 3x4–5 @ 8.5–9.
- Day 5 Upper: OHP 2x1 @ 8.5, then 4x2 @ 8.5; Close-Grip Bench 3x3–5 @ 8.5; Horizontal Row 3x6–8 @ 8.5.
- Optional Day 6: 20–30 min Z1–2 + mobility. Day 7: Rest.

Week 8 (Jul 20–26) Deload
- Main lifts to RPE 6–7, ~60% volume. Power 2–3x3 light. Aerobic: Zone 2 only, 25–35 min 1–2x/week. Accessories 2–3x8–10 @ RPE 6–7.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength-endurance and performance
Week 9 (Jul 27–Aug 2)
- Day 1 Lower Vol: Back Squat 4x5 @ 7–8; Tempo RDL 3x6 (3 s down) @ 7; Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8/side; Leg Press 3x10; Hanging Knee Raise 3x10–12.
- Day 2 Upper Vol: Bench 4x5 @ 7–8; Chest-Supported Row 4x8 @ 7–8; DB Incline 3x8–10; Pull-Up 3x5–6 (or BW AMRAP-1); Face Pull 3x12–15; Cable Chop 3x10/side.
- Day 3 Aerobic: 10x45 s @ RPE 7.5–8 / 75 s easy; cool-room only.
- Day 4 Lower Hinge: Deadlift 4x3 @ 8; Front Squat 3x5 @ 7–8; Hip Thrust 3x8 @ 7–8; Ham Curl 3x10–12; Calf 3x12–15; Farmer Carry 3x40–60 m.
- Day 5 Upper OH/Accessory: OHP 4x4 @ 8; Lat Pulldown 3x8–10; Close-Grip Bench 3x6–8; 1-Arm Cable Row 3x10/side; Rear Delt + Lateral Raise giant set 2–3 rounds.
- Optional Day 6: Zone 2 30–45 min + mobility. Day 7 Rest.

Week 10 (Aug 3–9)

Week 9 (Jul 27–Aug 2)
Day 1 Lower (volume)
- Back Squat 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
- Tempo RDL (3-sec eccentric) 3x6 @ RPE 7
- Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8/side
- Leg Press 3x10
- Core: Hanging Knee Raise 3x10–12

Day 2 Upper (volume)
- Bench Press 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
- Chest-Supported Row 4x8 @ RPE 7–8
- DB Incline Press 3x8–10

Here’s a focused nutrition plan to support training, mitigate perimenopausal symptoms (especially vasomotor), and protect bone health across the 12-week program. It includes daily targets, peri-workout strategy, bone- and cardio‑metabolic–supportive nutrients, sample day menus, and adjustments for symptom flare days and travel. Non-prescriptive; defer to GP/dietitian for individual contraindications (e.g., thyroid meds, kidney disease).

Daily macro and calorie guidance
- Calories: Set to maintain or very slight surplus (+0–10%) if strength/hypertrophy is primary; slight deficit (−10%) only if body comp is a priority and symptoms/sleep are stable. Avoid aggressive cuts—they can worsen hot flashes and sleep.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (spread over 4 feedings). Include one pre‑bed serving (20–30 g) to support overnight recovery.
  - Perimenopause nuance: Aim for 0.4–0.55 g/kg per meal with 2–3 g leucine per feeding (e.g., 30–40 g from animal or leucine-fortified plant sources).
- Carbohydrate: 3–5 g/kg/day baseline; up to 5–6 g/kg on heavy training days if recovery/energy lag. Prefer low–moderate GI carbs around training to steady thermoregulation.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day (don’t drop <25% of total kcal). Emphasize mono- and omega‑3 fats for vasomotor and cardio‑metabolic health.

Peri-workout fueling (align with “no fasted HIIT in heat”)
- 60–120 min pre-lift: 
  - 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein + fluids/electrolytes.
  - Examples: Greek yogurt + banana + honey; turkey wrap; soy yogurt + granola + berries.
- During (sessions >60 min or high sweat rate):
  - 250–500 ml cool fluid per 20–30 min; add 300–600 mg sodium/L. For long/heavy sessions, 20–30 g carbs/h from drink/chews.
- Post (within 1–2 h): 
  - 30–45 g high-quality protein + 60–90 g carbs (adjust to goals), include sodium if sweat loss high.

Bone health priorities
- Calcium: 1,200 mg/day total (food first; supplement only to make up gaps, split doses ≤500–600 mg for absorption).
  - Food sources: dairy or fortified plant milks/yogurts, firm tofu (calcium‑set), canned salmon/sardines with bones, leafy greens (collards, kale), almonds.
- Vitamin D: Target 800–2,000 IU/day (per GP and labs). Test status if unknown.
- Protein distribution: Sufficient protein supports bone matrix; include collagen-rich foods (or 10–15 g collagen hydrolysate + 50 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-lifting for tendon/ligament support).
- Vitamin K2 (MK‑7): 90–180 mcg/day from foods (fermented foods, eggs, certain cheeses) or supplement if advised by GP, especially with osteoporosis risk.
- Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day (glycinate/citrate forms) supports bone and sleep.
- Potassium: 3,400–4,700 mg/day from whole foods (fruit, veg, beans, dairy) supports blood pressure and muscle function.

Vasomotor symptom and metabolic support
- Phytoestrogen foods: Include daily if tolerated—soy (tofu, tempeh, edamame), flaxseed (1–2 Tbsp ground), legumes. Evidence suggests modest hot flash reduction for some.
- Omega‑3s: 2–3 servings/week of oily fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) or 1–2 g/day EPA+DHA supplement. May modestly help vasomotor symptoms and cardiovascular markers.
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–40 ml/kg/day fluids baseline; add sodium with training (300–600 mg/L). Limit alcohol (can trigger hot flashes) and keep caffeine ≤200 mg/day if sensitive.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day for glycemic control, satiety, and lipid profile. Favor low‑GI carbs around workouts to reduce thermic spikes.
- Anti-inflammatory pattern: Emphasize Mediterranean-style diet—vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, nuts, extra-virgin olive oil, fish; limit ultra-processed foods.

Micronutrient checklist (daily or average over the week)
- Iron: Monitor if heavy periods—even advanced lifters can underfuel iron. Include red meat 1–2x/week or high‑iron plant combos + vitamin C; consider ferritin test if fatigue persists.
- B12: Ensure adequacy, especially if mostly plant-based (supplement 500–1,000 mcg/week or per labs).
- Iodine: 150 mcg/day (iodized salt or seafood), unless thyroid condition warrants modification.
- Zinc: 8–12 mg/day for recovery and immune function.

Supplements (optional, evidence-based; confirm with GP)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day; benefits strength, cognition, and possibly bone density.
- Vitamin D3: Dose per labs (see above).
- Calcium (citrate or carbonate): Only to close gaps to 1,200 mg/day.
- Omega‑3 (EPA/DHA): 1–2 g/day if fish intake low.
- Magnesium glycinate/citrate: 200–400 mg in the evening.
- Collagen hydrolysate: 10–15 g + 50 mg vitamin C pre-lift for connective tissue support.
- Protein powder (whey, casein, soy, or blended plant) to meet daily protein.
- Creatine note: Maintain hydration; no heat-specific contraindication when dosing standardly.

Symptom-aware adjustments
- High hot-flash day or poor sleep:
  - Reduce stimulants, favor cooler, hydrating foods (yogurt, smoothies, salads with added protein).
  - Front-load carbs earlier in the day, lighter evening meal to aid sleep.
  - Increase sodium and fluids slightly on heavy sweat days to reduce dizziness.
- GI comfort in heat:
  - Lower fat/fiber in the 2–3 h pre-lift window; shift fiber to earlier/later meals.
  - Choose chilled, easy-to-digest options (smoothies, cold oats, rice bowls).

Sample day menus (approx. 2,100–2,400 kcal for a 70–75 kg active female; scale to body mass and goals)
- Breakfast (cooling): Overnight oats with 250 ml calcium‑fortified soy milk, 30 g whey/soy isolate mixed in, 1 Tbsp ground flaxseed, berries; 1 kiwi. Coffee or tea as tolerated.
- Mid-morning: Greek yogurt (200 g) + honey + sliced almonds; 500 ml water with electrolytes if training later.
- Pre-workout (60–90 min before): Turkey and hummus wrap on wholegrain tortilla + banana; 300–500 ml cool water with electrolytes.
- During: 250–500 ml/h cool water; add 20–30 g carbs/h if session >75 min.
- Post-workout lunch: Salmon rice bowl—150 g cooked salmon, 1 cup cooked jasmine rice, mixed greens/cucumber/edamame, avocado, sesame, soy-ginger dressing; calcium-fortified iced green tea.
- Afternoon: Cottage cheese (200 g) with pineapple; or tofu pudding with cocoa and maple syrup.
- Dinner: Chicken thigh or tempeh, roasted potatoes, sautéed collards (calcium source), olive oil; side salad with chickpeas and feta.
- Pre-bed: Casein shake or soy milk + protein (25–30 g) or skyr + berries; magnesium glycinate.

Plant-forward variation
- Swap dairy for calcium-fortified plant milks/yogurts.
- Protein anchors: tofu/tempeh/edamame, lentil pasta, seitan, soy isolate shakes; add B12 supplement; ensure calcium-set tofu.

Weekly planning tips
- Batch-cook proteins and grains; keep chilled grab-and-go options for heat waves (yogurt cups, protein puddings, sandwiches, cut fruit).
- Keep an electrolyte plan for every training session; store low-sugar electrolyte tabs in the gym bag.
- Track: morning body weight (trend), symptom frequency, sleep quality, and training performance; adjust carbs and sodium to stabilize energy and reduce overheating.

Red flags and medical notes
- If taking thyroid, osteoporosis, or blood pressure medications, coordinate timing with calcium/iron supplements (they can impair absorption)—typically separate by 3–4 hours.
- If hot flashes worsen with alcohol or spicy foods, limit around evening hours.
- If ferritin <30 ng/mL with fatigue, discuss iron supplementation and dosing with GP.

This nutrition plan aligns with the training blocks, supports bone density and connective tissue, helps manage vasomotor symptoms, and is practical in warmer conditions. Adjust quantities to body mass and goals; keep food choices enjoyable and sustainable.

Autoregulation and symptom-aware rules
- High-symptom or poor-sleep day: Cap main lifts at RPE 7; remove 1 set per main lift; swap intervals for 30–40 min Zone 2.
- Mid-set hot flash: Safely rack, cool (palms/neck 60–90 s), reduce next set by 2–5% or −1 rep.
- Intervals: Terminate if HR fails to recover to ≤70% HRmax before next rep.
- Weekly review of sleep, hot-flash frequency, session RPE; adjust loads/volume 5–10% as needed.

Equipment and environment
- Climate-controlled gym; breathable clothing; chalk for pulls; fans available.
- Keep cold towel/ice pack and chilled bottle for palm/neck cooling.

Outcome expectations
- Phase 1: Rebuild volume and tissue tolerance; symptom-aware pacing.
- Phase 2: Strong neural drive with safe heavy exposures; power maintained.
- Phase 3: Work-capacity bump with strength retention; option to estimate or lightly test 1RM in Week 12 under guardrails.
